subject: Human Evolution
title: Starch Digestion
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Starch Digestion.

hook.text: You have more copies of the amylase gene than a chimpanzee. That lets you break down starch faster.

buildup.text: Amylase in saliva begins carbohydrate digestion the moment food enters your mouth.

discovery.text: Populations with starch-rich diets—like farming cultures—carry more amylase gene copies than hunter-gatherers.

twist.text: This gene duplication may have occurred recently, tracking the rise of grain-based agriculture.

climax.text: Diet didn't just shape behavior—it literally copied and pasted genes in response to new foods.

quiz.question: Why do some humans have more amylase gene copies?
options: Starch-heavy diets selected for faster starch digestion
It's the same across all humans
